newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee closes at 35.71/72 against firm dollar.
newsitem.headline: India rupee closes at 35.71/72 against firm dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.71/72 to a dollar on Tuesday, compared to the opening level of 35.69/70, dealers said.
Soon after opening the strong demand for dollars seen over the past few days asserted itself nudging the rupee to 35.71/72 level, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
A leading Calcutta-based bank bought at this level, he said.
Continued dollar demand weakened the rupee in afternoon trade to the day's low of 35.7325 per dollar, dealers said. Most of the day's deals were at 35.7200/7250, they said.
Dollar supplies towards the close enabled the rupee to end the day at 35.717/727 per dollar.
"The underlying sentiment is one of persisting demand (for dollars)," said a dealer at a state-run bank in Bombay.
"It (heightened dollar demand) is continuing, though supplies matched demand today," he said.
One dealer said 35.70 appeared to be the new benchmark. "The rupee may see the 35.75 level if the tend continues."

Premia edged up on the forward dollar market in the morning on the back of a spurt in overnight call rates and a weakening of the rupee in the spot dollar market, but fell back towards the close, dealers said.
The six month annualised premia closed at 5.90 percent, compared to Monday's closing rate of 5.71 percent.
